headline: Large Energy Users Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, primarily data centers, bear the costs of new grid infrastructure necessitated by their demand, rather than socializing these costs across all ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Governor's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: SCC Requires Data Centers to Pay for New Transmission Infrastructure
news_summary: The State Corporation Commission (SCC) ordered Dominion Energy to develop a policy to directly assign the cost of transmission infrastructure to data centers and other large-load users. This decision, influenced by the Governor's administration, is projected to save Virginians hundreds of millions of dollars by shifting these costs from residential ratepayers to the large energy users who necessitate the upgrades.

headline: Data Centers Report Water Usage
short_summary: This bill mandates water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and providing critical data for water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, local governments, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden/potential scrutiny).
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Water Use by Data Centers
news_summary: The Virginia General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers. This legislation aims to address concerns about the lack of centralized tracking of data center water use, particularly as the industry expands and draws millions of gallons daily from municipal systems.

headline: Localities Regulate Data Center Siting, Noise
short_summary: This bill empowers localities to require site assessments for noise impacts and other environmental effects before approving new high energy use facilities, giving communities more control over data center development.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
news_headline: Virginia Data Center Legislation: Tax, Energy & Siting
news_summary: HB 153, passed by the legislature, establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities (HEUF) and requires zoning applicants to conduct site assessments examining a facility's sound profile on homes and schools within 500 feet. Localities can also require assessments of potential impacts on ground and surface water, agriculture, and historic resources.
